brief_bullets: France has reported its first-ever human case of the livestock pathogen Shamonda virus in a patient who subsequently died. Public health investigators are currently working to determine the precise route of transmission and whether the virus directly contributed to the fatality. Conventionally known as an animal virus affecting livestock, this unprecedented human infection has triggered heightened surveillance by health authorities. Experts are assessing the potential zoonotic risks and evaluating whether the pathogen poses a broader threat to public health and veterinary safety.
why_it_matters_bullets: This first documented human case signals a concerning potential spillover of a livestock virus into human populations.

stories.primary_headline: Latest estimate for Starship launches required to support a Moon landing? 22.

primary_source.headline: Latest estimate for Starship launches required to support a Moon landing? 22.
primary_source.content:
NASA does not have, nor want, nuclear weapons. But when it comes to a particular metric that is part of the Artemis Program to land people on the Moon, NASA guards a particular number like they are trying to prevent outsiders from cracking nuclear codes.
I am speaking of the number of Starship launches required to fuel a Starship-based lunar lander in low-Earth orbit such that it can fly out to the Moon, land there, and return to lunar orbit.
This number has been a moving target over the years. The general response from NASA has typically been, 'We don't know for sure, so we're not going to say.' In 2023, for example, the then-director of NASA's Human Landing System, Lisa Watson-Morgan, told Ars, "We have a general idea, but I’m reluctant to say exactly what that is."Read full article

stories.primary_headline: Prince William makes surprise appearance on Graham Norton Show

primary_source.headline: Prince William makes surprise appearance on Graham Norton Show
primary_source.content: During the episode, which airs on Friday, he joined Cate Blanchett, Robert Irwin and Hannah Waddingham, who are all involved with the prize. As Norton spoke about the initiative with the trio he surprised the audience by then inviting the prince out to join them on the sofa, to cheers and gasps from the audience. They discussed the need to pair optimism and urgency when tackling climate change. The prize was founded by William to "celebrate and scale the solutions that will repair our planet". The guests also chatted about William's long-time support for Aston Villa, and his love of Christopher Nolan films. William set up the Earthshot Prize in 2020, drawing inspiration from US President John F Kennedy's Moonshot project, which challenged scientists to get astronauts to the Moon and back safely. There are five Earthshots, or goals, for which an award is given: Protect and Restore Nature, Clean Our Air, Revive Our Oceans, Build a Waste-Free World and Fix Our Climate. Each winner receives £1m.

stories.primary_headline: HeLa to a new world where progress in science matches dignity for patient

primary_source.headline: HeLa to a new world where progress in science matches dignity for patient
primary_source.content: The omission of Henrietta Lacks, who donated the immortal cells that have facilitated biomedical research, from scientific history is a rare wrong that has been righted, recently. Thanks to the battle her family fought, today, more regulations will govern ethical research.

sources.headline: HeLa to a new world where progress in science matches dignity for patient

brief_bullets: Henrietta Lacks, an African American woman whose cervical cancer cells were harvested without her knowledge in 1951, has finally received historical and institutional recognition following a relentless advocacy campaign by her descendants. The landmark settlement between the Lacks family and biotechnology giant Thermo Fisher Scientific rectifies decades of medical exploitation that birthed the immortal HeLa cell line, which fundamentally transformed global biomedical research, vaccine development, and oncology. This watershed moment highlights systemic historical injustices in medical ethics while catalyzing modern institutional reforms to ensure patient consent, transparency, and dignity govern contemporary scientific research and commercialization practices.
why_it_matters_bullets: This milestone reshapes bioethical standards by reinforcing patient consent requirements and corporate accountability in biomedical research.

stories.primary_headline: How citizen science is tracking changes in shorelines around the world

primary_source.headline: How citizen science is tracking changes in shorelines around the world
primary_source.content: An app and a camera phone are all that’s needed at more than 200 spots to help researchers monitor coastal areasThe shoreline changes with the weather. Tracking these changes over time is a labour-intensive task, and an army of citizen scientists with camera phones is a great asset.The CoastSnap project started in Australia in 2017 and has spread to beaches worldwide. You may have spotted the setup while out walking along the coast: a cradle to rest your phone on while taking a picture and a sign explaining where to send the snap. Continue reading...

sources.headline: How citizen science is tracking changes in shorelines around the world

brief_bullets: The global CoastSnap initiative leverages crowdsourced smartphone photography across more than two hundred international locations to monitor rapid shoreline changes driven by weather and environmental shifts. Initiated in Australia in 2017, the project utilizes standardized camera cradles and community participation to overcome the labor-intensive hurdles historically faced by coastal researchers. By gathering consistent visual data from everyday beachgoers, scientists can better track erosion patterns and coastal vulnerabilities without relying exclusively on expensive, dedicated monitoring equipment. This collaborative model demonstrates how public engagement can effectively scale data collection for critical climate and geographic research.
why_it_matters_bullets: Crowdsourcing coastal monitoring democratizes vital climate data, empowering researchers to track environmental shifts at an unprecedented global scale.

primary_source.content: The incident prompted devotees who had consumed the 'charanamrit' during Durga Puja to seek vaccination as a precaution.

sources.headline: 450 Get Anti-Rabies Vaccine After Consuming Milk From Suspected Rabid Cow

brief_bullets: Following a Durga Puja ritual in India, approximately 450 devotees received anti-rabies vaccinations after consuming 'charanamrit'—a sacred offering containing milk—derived from a cow later suspected of having rabies. Local health authorities and temple organizers acted swiftly to administer post-exposure prophylaxis to all potentially exposed individuals to prevent fatal viral transmission. While no infections have been confirmed yet, the massive preventative intervention highlights severe bio-security vulnerabilities in traditional communal food practices during religious gatherings, sparking urgent calls for rigorous veterinary screening of dairy livestock.
why_it_matters_bullets: This incident exposes critical food safety risks in religious rituals, demanding mandatory veterinary checks for temple livestock.

primary_source.content: The beloved high school TV show is returning in a different political climate. I’m skeptical that Ryan Murphy has the nuance this moment needsFor months, Ryan Murphy has been discussing Glee. In July, he expressed his love for the musical comedy drama he created. In September, he said that he had finished writing a pilot for a potential reboot, adding that he had reached out to some of the cast about a reunion. And now it is official: Disney+ and Hulu have commissioned a Glee revival.Glee, which ran for six seasons between 2009 and 2015, was a cultural juggernaut during its initial tenure. The show won six Emmys, four Golden Globes and made stars of actors including Lea Michele, Jonathan Groff, Chris Colfer, Darren Criss and the late Cory Monteith and Naya Rivera. Centred on the trials of New Directions, a scrappy show choir at the fictional McKinley high school in Ohio, the show became known for its peppy covers of show tunes, 80s power pop hits such as Journey’s Don’t Stop Believin’ (a Glee signature), 2010s chart-toppers and some truly baffling mashups (the amalgamation of Scissor Sisters’ Let’s Have a Kiki and Turkey Lurkey Time from Promises, Promises remains … a choice).
